subject: ela
intro: Read each passage carefully. These tasks ask you to infer the theme from how events and characters develop, connect a specific detail to the theme, and build or judge objective summaries. Use evidence from the whole passage, and remember that a theme is a message about life, not a one-word topic or a retelling of the plot.

items.prompt:
Read the passage, then write a one-sentence statement of its theme.

Devon had practiced his speech for weeks, but when he stepped on stage his mind went blank. The audience waited. He thought about running off, but instead he took a slow breath and admitted, "I forgot my opening line." A few people chuckled kindly. Then, calmer, he began again and finished strong. Afterward, his teacher told him the honest pause was the most powerful part. Devon realized that the moment he stopped trying to hide his mistake was the moment he actually connected with the crowd.

Write a complete sentence that states the theme (the message about life this passage teaches). Do not just give a topic word.
items.answer: Admitting a mistake honestly can build a stronger connection than hiding it.

steps: Identify what changes in the passage: Devon goes from wanting to hide his blank moment to openly admitting it.
Notice the result of his choice: the honest pause is what connects him to the audience and lets him finish strong.
Turn that pattern into a general life lesson rather than a plot summary or a single topic word like 'honesty.'
A strong theme statement: Admitting a mistake honestly can build a stronger connection than hiding it.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

For years, Mr. Alvarez let the empty lot beside his house grow wild. Neighbors complained, but he said the weeds were nobody's business. One spring, a family of foxes made a den there, and children gathered each evening to watch the kits play. When the city announced plans to pave the lot for parking, it was Mr. Alvarez, of all people, who organized the petition to save it. "I never thought anyone cared about that scrap of land," he admitted, "least of all me."

The theme of this passage is that people can come to value what they once ignored. Which detail from the passage BEST conveys that theme? Explain your choice in one or two sentences.
items.answer: The detail that Mr. Alvarez, who once said the lot was nobody's business, organizes the petition to save it best conveys the theme, because his shift from ignoring the lot to fighting for it shows him valuing what he once dismissed.

steps: The theme is that people can come to value what they once ignored, so look for a detail showing a change from ignoring to valuing.
Early in the passage Mr. Alvarez calls the lot 'nobody's business,' showing he ignored it.
By the end he organizes the petition to save it and admits he never thought he cared, showing he now values it.
That reversal in his own behavior is the clearest evidence of the theme, more than the foxes or the children, who are background details.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The relay team was sure they would lose. Their fastest runner, Priya, had sprained her ankle the day before, so slower Joon would run the final leg. During the race, the other three runners pushed harder than ever to give Joon a lead. He could hear them shouting his name as he took the baton. Joon did not run his fastest time, but he held the lead his teammates had built, and the team won by a step. "We never could have done it as four separate runners," Priya said.

Write an objective summary of this passage in two or three sentences. Include the key events in order and leave out any opinions or judgments.
items.answer: The relay team expected to lose after their fastest runner, Priya, sprained her ankle and slower Joon had to run the final leg. The other three runners pushed hard to give Joon a lead, and although Joon did not run his fastest, he held that lead. The team won by a step, and Priya noted they could not have done it as separate runners.

steps: List the key events in order: Priya's injury forces Joon onto the final leg; the team expects to lose; the other runners build a lead for Joon; Joon holds the lead; the team wins narrowly.
State each event factually, using only what the text says.
Leave out opinions such as calling the win amazing or the team brave; report only what happened and what Priya said.
Combine the events into two or three sequenced sentences for an objective summary.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Nadia had always copied her older brother's answers on homework, telling herself it saved time. When their parents signed them both up for a coding club, the projects could not be copied; each member had to build their own. The first weeks were miserable. Nadia's programs crashed again and again while her brother's worked. But slowly she learned to read the error messages, and by the showcase her game ran smoothly. "I used to think shortcuts were smart," she told her brother. "Now I see they just delayed the part where I actually learned."

A student wrote this theme: "Coding is difficult for beginners." Explain why this is not the best statement of the theme, and write a better one.
items.answer: "Coding is difficult for beginners" only restates a surface detail and does not capture the lesson about Nadia's growth. A better theme is that avoiding hard work through shortcuts only delays real learning.

steps: Check whether 'Coding is difficult for beginners' is a message about life or just a detail from the plot. It is only a detail and ignores Nadia's change.
Trace what Nadia learns: copying saved time but kept her from learning, while struggling on her own finally taught her.
A theme should generalize that lesson beyond coding.
Better theme: Avoiding hard work through shortcuts only delays real learning.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The lighthouse keeper, old Bram, had not spoken to the villagers in years, blaming them for a quarrel no one else remembered. One stormy night, a fishing boat lost its way near the rocks. Bram could have stayed angry behind his door. Instead he climbed the tower and worked the great lamp through the night, sweeping its beam across the water until every fisherman was safe ashore. In the morning, the villagers found warm bread left on his step, and for the first time in years, Bram opened the door to say thank you.

Which statement is the theme, and which is only the topic? Label each.
Statement 1: Forgiveness
Statement 2: Choosing to help others can begin to heal an old grudge.
items.answer: Statement 1 (Forgiveness) is the topic. Statement 2 (Choosing to help others can begin to heal an old grudge) is the theme.

steps: A topic is usually a single word or short label naming a subject; a theme is a full sentence stating a message about life.
Statement 1, 'Forgiveness,' is a one-word subject, so it is the topic.
Statement 2 is a complete sentence describing a lesson the events teach, so it is the theme.
The passage supports the theme: Bram helps the village, and the grudge begins to heal when he opens his door.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Every autumn, Tomas entered the town's pie contest and lost to Mrs. Healy, whose crust was famous. This year he decided to learn rather than just compete. He visited Mrs. Healy and asked how she made her crust. She laughed and taught him her trick with cold butter. At the contest, Mrs. Healy won again, but Tomas placed second for the first time ever. "You should have kept your secret," a neighbor told Mrs. Healy. She shook her head. "A recipe shared comes back to me every time someone bakes it," she said.

The theme is that sharing what you know can be more rewarding than guarding it. Which detail BEST develops this theme? Name the detail and explain in one sentence.
items.answer: Mrs. Healy's reply, "A recipe shared comes back to me every time someone bakes it," best develops the theme because it directly states the value she finds in sharing her knowledge rather than guarding it.

steps: The theme is that sharing knowledge can be more rewarding than guarding it, so look for a detail that shows a character valuing sharing.
Tomas placing second is a result, but it is about him, not about the reward of sharing.
Mrs. Healy's line about the recipe coming back to her directly expresses the lesson that sharing is rewarding.
That line of dialogue is the strongest detail conveying the theme.

items.prompt:
Read the passage and the draft summary.

Passage: When the river flooded, the Okafor family had to leave their home with only what they could carry. They sheltered at the school gym for two weeks. Neighbors they barely knew brought blankets, food, and a chess set for the children. When the water finally fell and the family returned to clean up, the same neighbors came to help haul out the ruined furniture. "We lost a lot," Mr. Okafor said quietly, "but we found out we were never really alone."

Draft summary: A river flooded and forced the Okafor family to leave home. They stayed at the school gym, where kind and generous neighbors helped them, which was really heartwarming. When the water fell, those neighbors helped them clean up, and Mr. Okafor said they were never really alone.

Identify the phrase in the draft summary that is a personal opinion rather than an objective statement, and rewrite that sentence so it is objective.
items.answer: The opinion phrase is "which was really heartwarming" (and the judgment word "kind and generous"). An objective rewrite: "They stayed at the school gym, where neighbors brought them blankets, food, and a chess set."

steps: An objective summary reports only what happened, with no reactions or judgments.
Scan the draft for words that express the writer's feeling: 'really heartwarming' is a reaction, and 'kind and generous' is a judgment about the neighbors.
Remove those words and replace them with the factual actions from the passage.
Objective rewrite: 'They stayed at the school gym, where neighbors brought them blankets, food, and a chess set.'

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Lin wanted the lead in the school play more than anything, and so did her best friend, Carmen. When the cast list went up, Carmen had won the part. Lin felt the sting of disappointment, but she also saw Carmen standing alone, nervously reading the long script. That night Lin almost did not text her. Then she remembered all the lines they had practiced together. She sent the message: "You'll be amazing. Want help running lines?" Carmen wrote back within seconds: "I was so afraid you'd be mad. Yes, please."

Write a one-sentence theme statement for this passage. Make sure it is a message about life, not a topic word or a retelling of the plot.
items.answer: Choosing to support a friend can matter more than winning what you wanted for yourself.

steps: Identify the central choice: Lin is disappointed she lost the role but decides to help Carmen anyway.
Notice the outcome: her message eases Carmen's fear and keeps their friendship strong.
Generalize this into a life lesson rather than naming a topic like 'friendship' or restating that Lin texted Carmen.
Theme: Choosing to support a friend can matter more than winning what you wanted for yourself.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The young king inherited a treasury full of gold and a kingdom short on bread. His advisers urged him to build a golden statue of himself so the people would feel proud. Instead, the king emptied half the treasury to buy grain and seed for the farmers. The advisers warned he would be forgotten without a monument. Years later, travelers passing through the well-fed, peaceful land asked who had ruled so wisely, and every farmer knew his name without a single statue ever being raised.

The theme is that true and lasting respect is earned through actions that help others, not through displays of wealth. Which detail BEST conveys this theme? Name the detail and explain why in one sentence.
items.answer: The detail that the king empties half the treasury to buy grain and seed instead of building a statue of himself best conveys the theme, because his choice to help the people rather than display his wealth is exactly what earns him lasting respect.

steps: The theme contrasts helping others with displaying wealth, so the best detail must show that contrast in the king's action.
The golden statue represents a display of wealth; spending the treasury on grain represents helping others.
The king's decision to buy grain and seed instead of the statue is the decisive choice that reveals the theme.
The later fame is the result, but the choice itself is the detail that conveys the lesson.

items.prompt:
Read the passage and the two draft summaries.

Passage: Determined to prove she could camp alone, Reza set out for the mountain trail. By dusk she realized she had forgotten her tent stakes, and the wind was rising. She nearly turned back in defeat. Instead, she gathered fallen branches and rigged a shelter, lashing the tent to a low tree. It was not perfect, and she slept little, but in the morning her shelter still stood. She walked home tired but certain she could solve problems she had not planned for.

Summary A: Reza went camping alone, forgot her tent stakes, built a shelter from branches when the wind rose, and returned home certain she could handle unexpected problems.
Summary B: Reza foolishly forgot her stakes, but she made a messy shelter anyway and went home.

Which summary is the objective and complete one? Explain what is wrong with the other summary.
items.answer: Summary A is the objective and complete summary. Summary B is flawed because it inserts the opinion "foolishly" and the judgment "messy," and it omits the key idea that Reza learned she could handle unexpected problems.

steps: Check each summary for opinions: Summary B uses 'foolishly' and 'messy,' which are judgments, not facts.
Check each summary for completeness: Summary B leaves out the resolution where Reza gains confidence to handle unplanned problems.
Summary A states the key events in order with no opinions and includes the resolution.
Therefore Summary A is the objective, complete summary.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Marcus bragged that he never needed maps; he trusted his sense of direction. On the class hike, he ignored the trail markers and led his small group on a shortcut. An hour later they were standing in a meadow none of them recognized. The others were frightened, and Marcus felt his confidence drain away. Quietly, he pulled out the map he had stuffed in his pack and never opened. Together they traced their location and found the path again. Marcus did not say much, but he kept the map in his hand the rest of the day.

A student wrote this theme: "Marcus should have used his map." Explain why this theme is too narrow, and write a stronger one.
items.answer: "Marcus should have used his map" is too narrow because it applies only to Marcus and this one hike rather than stating a general lesson. A stronger theme is that overconfidence can lead us astray, and being willing to rely on guidance helps us find our way.

steps: A good theme applies broadly, not just to one character in one situation.
'Marcus should have used his map' names only Marcus and the specific map, so it is too narrow.
Find the general lesson: Marcus's overconfidence got the group lost, and using the map (guidance) got them back.
Stronger theme: Overconfidence can lead us astray, and being willing to rely on guidance helps us find our way.

items.prompt:
Read the poem.

The little seed lay in the dark,
afraid to split its sturdy shell.
"Stay safe," it whispered to itself,
"down here where I have always dwelled."

But roots grow restless in the cold,
and something pressed it toward the light.
It cracked, it ached, it pushed, it climbed,
and met the morning, green and bright.

Write a one-sentence theme statement for this poem. Make sure it expresses a message about life rather than simply describing a seed.
items.answer: Growth often requires leaving the safety of the familiar and pushing through discomfort.

steps: Notice the poem is about a seed but works as a comparison for any kind of growth.
Trace the change: the seed is afraid and wants to stay safe, then cracks and pushes upward despite the ache.
Translate that into a lesson about life, not a literal description of a plant.
Theme: Growth often requires leaving the safety of the familiar and pushing through discomfort.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The two shopkeepers, Dara and Sims, had competed on the same street for twenty years, each certain the other was the enemy. When a fire swept through the block one night, Dara's store was spared but Sims's was gutted. Everyone expected Dara to gloat. Instead, the next morning, Dara cleared a corner of his own shop and hung a sign: "Sims and Sons, temporary location, ask inside." Customers were stunned. "Twenty years we fought," Dara said with a shrug, "but I'd rather have a neighbor than an empty lot."

Write an objective summary of this passage in two or three sentences. Keep it accurate and free of opinions.
items.answer: Dara and Sims had run competing shops on the same street for twenty years, each seeing the other as an enemy. After a fire destroyed Sims's store but spared Dara's, Dara cleared a corner of his own shop and put up a sign offering Sims a temporary location. Dara explained that he would rather have a neighbor than an empty lot.

steps: List the key events in order: long rivalry, fire that spares Dara but ruins Sims, Dara offering Sims space, Dara's explanation.
State each event using only the facts in the text.
Avoid opinions such as calling Dara generous or the act surprising; the customers' shock is in the text, but the summary should not add the writer's own judgment.
Combine the facts into two or three sequenced sentences.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

When the science fair winners were announced, Ivy's name was not among them, even though she had worked harder than anyone. She watched a classmate who had barely started the day before walk up with a ribbon for a flashy but simple project. Anger rose in her throat. Then her teacher pulled her aside. "Your data was the most careful I saw," she said. "Ribbons fade. The way you think will carry you for years." Ivy was still disappointed, but she folded the comment into her pocket like something worth keeping.

Which statement BEST expresses the theme, and why is the other only a plot detail?
Statement 1: Ivy did not win a ribbon at the science fair.
Statement 2: The lasting value of careful work can outweigh a prize that quickly fades.
items.answer: Statement 2 best expresses the theme. Statement 1 is only a plot detail because it merely reports one event that happened rather than stating a message about life.

steps: A theme is a general message about life; a plot detail just reports what happened.
Statement 1 reports a single event (Ivy did not win), so it is a plot detail.
Statement 2 expresses a broader lesson supported by the teacher's words about ribbons fading while careful thinking lasts.
Therefore Statement 2 is the theme and Statement 1 is only a plot detail.

items.prompt:
Read the passage and the draft summary.

Passage: Grandpa Otis kept a battered toolbox he refused to replace, even after the latch broke and the handle wore smooth. One summer, Mia asked why he did not just buy a new one. He opened it and showed her the tools inside, each one a gift or a hand-me-down: his father's hammer, a wrench from his first job, a chisel a friend had left him. "The box is nothing," he said. "It's what it carries, and who gave it, that I won't throw away." Mia never asked about the toolbox again.

Draft summary: Grandpa Otis kept an old, ugly toolbox because the tools inside were gifts and hand-me-downs from people in his life, and he valued the memories more than a new box. Mia stopped asking about it.

Identify the one word in the draft summary that makes it less objective, and explain why an objective summary should not include it.
items.answer: The word "ugly" makes the summary less objective. An objective summary should not include it because "ugly" is a personal judgment about the toolbox's appearance, not a fact stated in the passage, which only describes the box as battered and worn.

steps: An objective summary reports facts from the text without the writer's opinions.
Scan the draft for evaluative words: 'old' is supported by the text, but 'ugly' is a personal judgment.
The passage describes the box as battered and worn, but never calls it ugly, so that word adds opinion.
Removing 'ugly' keeps the summary objective and faithful to the passage.
